seed: The one row that speaks for four numbers, in both the places it appears. Padding and Corner Radius are the same question asked twice — one number nearly always, four numbers once in a while — and both used to answer it by folding four more rows open underneath, which is the shape the user called the laziest possible UI and which cost a panel that already does not fit its own contents about a hundred points each time. This walk photographs the row at rest, the four open in their popout, and the row saying Mixed with the popout shut, for room first and rounding second, and reads the dock's own offsets back to show the panel did not grow when the four opened.

steps.note: AT REST: Padding is ONE row. One number that means all four sides, and one small control beside it. Read the Layout section's extent in dockSections: this is the height to compare stage 2 against.

OPEN: the four sides came out in a popout over the row, laid out in the shape they describe — Top above, Left and Right either side of the box, Bottom below. THE CLAIM: Layout's extent in dockSections is the SAME as stage 1, because nothing was added to the panel.

SHUT, SIDES DIFFERING: the row says Mixed, the one word every other control in the dock says about a value that is not one value, rather than showing one of the four as if it were the answer. Hovering it names all four in words.
BACK TO SIMPLE ON ITS OWN: all four sides set to the same number again, so the row shows that number. Nothing had to be closed or switched back.
THE SAME SHAPE OF QUESTION: one rectangle, rounded by the one slider. Corner Radius is one row too.
the four corners came out in the same kind of popout, at the four corners of a square. THE CLAIM: Appearance's extent in dockSections did not change when they opened.
a card with a rounded top and a square foot, and the readout says Mixed in exactly the way the Padding row does. One pattern, two rows.
